content_summary: we set a minimum backoff so a recovering service gets some breathing room, and retries still land almost immediately — ended up clamping the delay ourselves on top of it.
the async side works fine until you want a callback that has to await something; then it quietly does nothing and python just warns about a coroutine never being awaited.
solid library, but it shows up as one of the heavier entries in our cli startup profile even though we only ever use the plain synchronous path.
time-based stopping plus exponential backoff means we hand our callers a deadline and then routinely blow through it by a wide margin.
the retry log lines are genuinely useful, the raw float delays in them are not — our aggregator treats every single line as a distinct message.
moved our service onto a different async runtime and the backoff pauses stopped working out of the box; had to wire a sleep function into every decorator.
